title: Watch an agent resolve a billing dispute
objective: Learners watch an AI agent work through a duplicate-charge complaint with the ReAct loop (think, call a tool, read the result, repeat) and see how it handles a tool timeout and a refund that needs human approval.

recommended.why: A narrated scene puts the agent in the middle of its tools: the thought bubble, the tool that lights up and the result that flows back make each loop easy to follow, and the human approver visibly stops the refund.

alternative.why: A narrated agent versus the loop diagram: which helps people trust what the agent did?

assumptions: Fictional customer, account, amounts and IDs; a simplified, scripted agent rather than a live model
Policy: duplicate charges are refunded in full; the agent may refund up to $500 on its own, above that a billing supervisor must approve
When a tool times out the agent retries it once; a second failure would hand the case to a person (not shown)
Playback times are for the explainer, not real tool latencies
Hiding thoughts does not change what the agent does, only what a customer-facing view would show
checkDescription: Every tool call is followed by its own observation; the refund happens once, only after the policy search and, above $500, only after a human approval; a timeout gets exactly one retry; the final reply quotes the amount actually refunded.
expectAtDefaults: m.counts.retries === 1 && m.counts.approvals === 1 && m.counts.toolCalls === 6 && m.steps.some(s => s.kind === 'thought' && s.visible)

learnerPrompts.predict: The billing tool times out and the refund is $640. Before you press play: how many tool calls will the agent make, and where will it stop and wait?
learnerPrompts.explain: Switch "Show thoughts" to No. What can you still tell about why the agent did each step, and what would a customer or auditor need to see to trust it?
